To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(AC/GT)n repeats are located near breakpoints of rearrangements in Drosophil melanogaster.
the T(1,2)dor(var)7 rearrangement in Drosophla melanogaster is associated with the presence of a (AC/GT)(n) repeat and a T-rich sequence in the vicinity of the breakpoint.
the distribution of (AC/ GT) repeats coincided the location of half of the mapped breakpoints in the X-chromosome of melanogaster.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of (AC/GC) minisatellites in the formation of the T(2;1)dor(var7)-induced position effect in D. melanogaster.
the search of the sequence of the DNA in the region of breakpoint of the rearrangement inducing the mosaic-type effect.
the analysis of the DNA sequences in the region of T(1; 2)dor(var 7) translocation, which causes a position effect in D. melanogaster.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T(1:2)dor(var 7) translocation breakpoint lies between the two (AC/GT)n repeats.
there is a correlation between (AC/GT)n minisatellite sequences and rearrangement breakpoints.
the T(1:2)dor(var)7 rearrangement is a result of a recombination between two sequences of the GTG(TT)n minisatellite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the (AC/GT)n minisatellite is a marker of rearrangements in the 2B region and is involved in the rearrangement of T(1; 2)dor(var 7) translocation.

(AC/GT)n repeats are located in the region of X-chromosomal breakpoint of T(1; 2)dor(var 7) and that the sequence of the pentanucleotide (CTGTT)n is similar to the GTGTT sequence of the satellite attached to the fragment 1A- 2B of the X-chromosome.
the T(1:2)dor(var 7) rearrangement occurred in the region of 2B-X chromosome, and the breakpoints of rearrangements are located in (AC/GT)n repeats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the (AC/GT)-minisatellite sequence is a hotspot of chromosomal breakage in D. melanogaster.
(AC/GT)n sequences are located in the vicinity of rearrangements breakpoints and that the T-rich sequences are also found in the vicinity of the breakpoints of the T(3;1)dor(var1) translocation.
the T-rich sequences and short tandem repeats may be involved in the formation of the rearrangements in the X-chromosome of the Drosophila.
